transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-23 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Maya (Shoreline CTO), Liam (Eng Lead), Priya (Data Eng)

Summary (auto): quick discovery - shorelines wants fast prototype but need security gating for later.

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:07] Maya (Shoreline): yep, loud and clear, thanks. we got the agenda you sent.
[00:12] Sofia: cool, i'll do a quick intro to redwood and then devon will jump into the tech, but first curious high level - maya, what are you hoping to get from this hour?
[00:27] Maya: yeah so we want to run a quick proof-of-concept to validate latency and cost for our search summarization flow. goal is to get to first call within a week ideally, we have an upcoming demo to execs. also need to surface any blockers for using hosted vs keeping it in our vpc.
[00:43] Liam: and to add, our infra team is strict about keys and data retention, so we need to know what the hosted isolation looks like, and if vpc/private is required down the road.
[00:55] Sofia: got it. typical -- sprint to first-call + runway for private. we often do a two-phase approach: PLG/self-serve hosted with credits to prove model/latency, then escalate to dedicated or private if compliance requires.
[01:12] Priya: how long does that hosted credit provisioning take?
[01:16] Sofia: usually same day if you have sign-up done; we can provision a 30k token credit code and a pre-configured sample repo.
[01:25] Maya: ok that lines up. devon, can you talk about how the hosted endpoint differs from a vpc private deploy from a network/security perspective?
[01:38] Devon (Redwood SE): sure, so hosted is our managed control plane + multi-tenant serving runtime. network path is outbound TLS to our api endpoints, ephemeral keys. for vpc/private we either provide a VPC peering endpoint or an on-prem appliance depending on needs — that gives you customer managed network, dedicated control plane, and no egress to public internet from model inference nodes.
[01:58] Liam: do you support bringing our own KMS? we need HSM-backed keys.
[02:03] Devon: yes we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations via partners). for private deployments key material can be fully customer-managed; on hosted we encrypt at rest and offer envelope encryption with a customer CMK for enterprise tiers.
[02:20] Maya: and audit logs? our compliance team will want immutable audit trails.
[02:24] Sofia: we have per-request audit logging available in enterprise plans, retention configurable. we can share SOC2 report and a sample audit log schema.
[02:34] Priya: perfect — can you share that?
[02:36] Sofia: yes, i'll attach security pack after.
[02:40] [00:03:10] (small cross talk)
[03:10] Devon: back to perf - what's your latency target?
[03:13] Maya: sub-600ms 95th p99-ish for short prompts (up to 512 tokens) in our interactive demo, cost per inference should be under $0.03 per call in prototype stage.
[03:28] Devon: ok that helps. on hosted we have model catalog with verified profiles; depending on which model you pick, you can hit 300-500ms p95 on GPU-backed variants. quantized variants lower cost but add latency variability.
[03:44] Liam: are there recommended models for low-latency summarization?
[03:47] Devon: yes, we typically recommend smaller encoder-decoder models tuned for latency or quantized key-value cache friendly decoders. i'll share our model guide with per-token cost and perf numbers.
[03:58] Maya: great — and what about continuous batching and its effect on latency? we don't want batching to introduce tail latencies for interactive demo.
[04:07] Devon: auto batching is adaptive; you can set latency SLOs that prioritize immediate dispatch over batch aggregation. for TTFT (time-to-first-token) sensitive flows we set a low target that disables large batch waits.
[04:22] Sofia: to be clear: for the sprint we can pre-configure an aggressive low-latency profile and demo e2e.
[04:29] Maya: timeline wise, we want a first call by next tuesday — is that realistic?
[04:34] Sofia: yes if you sign up or we give you a workspace, and we provision credits today, devon can run a smoke test with you and share a repo.
[04:41] Liam: sign-up is fine. i imagine we'll need a few service accounts and a network review.
[04:47] Priya: also curious about data retention on hosted — do you retain prompts or outputs?
[04:52] Devon: hosted by default doesn't persist prompts beyond 30 days for analytics unless you opt in. enterprise can turn off logging of user content completely, and dedicated/private gives you full control.
[05:05] Maya: ok, send those defaults in writing.
[05:07] Sofia: i will.
[05:09] [00:06:00] (pause as screenshare starts)
[06:00] Devon: i'll walk through a short sample repo — this is the quickstart: a small node/python script calling the redwood text generation endpoint. you'll see minimal config: api key, model, prompt.
[06:14] Devon: (shares link) https://redwood.example/quickstart/sample-repo — note that's a placeholder link we will replace with the customer-specific one.
[06:24] Liam: nice, does the sdk support streaming?
[06:27] Devon: yes streaming is supported via websockets/http chunking; we have both server-side and client-side libs.
[06:33] Priya: for our demo we want streaming to start rendering partial summary while tokens generate.
[06:38] Devon: that's a common pattern, we can set up the SDK to produce partial deltas.
[06:42] Maya: what does the quickstart include for benchmarking? simple latency, concurrency tests?
[06:48] Devon: sample gRPC/http scripts, a small load script that exercises single-threaded p95/p99 latency and a concurrency profile. for more depth we can run a 1k call warmup.
[06:58] Sofia: for the POC we usually recommend: 1) sign-up + credits, 2) baseline smoke test with SE, 3) run internal scenario with your data (anonymized) then pivot to dedicated if needed.
[07:12] Maya: curious about cost modeling — what levers should we tune to get below $0.03 per call?
[07:18] Devon: three levers: model choice (smaller model), quantization (8-bit/4-bit), and caching/prefix reuse to avoid recomputing repeated context. also request batching for background jobs.
[07:32] Priya: can we get guidance on tokenization and effective token counts — our current estimate is off.
[07:36] Devon: yes we'll share a tokenization guide plus a quick script to measure tokens.
[07:42] Maya: security again: does redwood support SAML SSO and RBAC for team access?
[07:47] Sofia: yes SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC with project-level roles on enterprise tiers.
[07:54] Liam: do you have a SOC2 report we can show to our compliance team?
[07:58] Sofia: yes, i'll attach our SOC2 and ISO docs.
[08:02] Maya: thanks.
[08:05] [00:09:00] (short snafu: software share glitch)
[09:00] Sofia: small hiccup — while we wait, quick qualification: what are your internal stakeholders and evaluation process? who signs off?
[09:11] Maya: product/CTO initially, then security + infra. final purchase probably by procurement. timeline: we want POC results in 2 weeks and a purchase decision within 6-8 weeks if all good.
[09:27] Sofia: good — that fits our usual cadence. we'll prepare an SOW-friendly pilot outline.
[09:33] Liam: any blockers for network egress? our infra will require an IP allowlist if hosted. is that supported?
[09:40] Devon: yes we publish egress IP ranges for allowlisting and have peering options for VPC.
[09:46] Priya: on observability, do you expose per-request tracing headers we can connect to our Sentry/NewRelic?
[09:52] Devon: yes we have tracing hooks and a request id you can pass through; we support OpenTelemetry in the control plane.
[09:59] Maya: ok, that's helpful.
[10:03] [00:11:30] Devon: quick note on fallback and graceful degradation — we support routing policies so if a higher-cost GPU pool is at capacity we can fallback to a smaller model variant. this prevents outages but may affect output quality.
[10:18] Sofia: that's one of our reliability differentiators — deterministic fallback policies.
[10:24] Liam: worth asking — do you support model version pinning per-route?
[10:28] Devon: yes. you can pin model version, rollout canary or A/B, and automatic fallback.
[10:33] Maya: what about data residency? we operate in europe and us, need to ensure EU data stays in EU.
[10:40] Devon: region pinning is supported, hosted regions include eu-west and us-central. private deployments can be on-prem for full residency.
[10:47] Sofia: ok, to make this concrete: we will provision a hosted workspace + 30k token credits, devon will run a 20min smoke benchmark with your sample prompt tomorrow, and we'll share security docs and hosting comparison.
[10:59] Maya: sounds good. please send the quickstart repo and the credits code.
[11:03] Sofia: will do.
[11:05] Priya: one last nit — how do you handle pii; should we tokenize or redact client ids before sending?
[11:11] Devon: for prototype, anonymize sensitive fields. if you go enterprise, we can enable on-host redaction hooks and field-level masking.
[11:20] Maya: ok good.
[11:23] [00:14:00] (closing)
[14:00] Sofia: recap of next steps: i'll send hosting comparison + security pack + credit code; devon will follow up with perf script and set the benchmark slot. schedule wise, how does tuesday morning look for the SE smoke test?
[14:14] Maya: tuesday 09:30 PT works.
[14:17] Sofia: great — i'll book it and include the pilot outline. thanks everyone.
[14:22] Liam: thanks.
[14:24] (end)

Auto sections: Questions captured: 
- Does Redwood support BYOK/HSM? (Answer: yes — enterprise/private)
- What are default data retention and logging policies? (Answer: hosted defaults 30d, configurable)

Notes about transcription: a few proper nouns mangled (ip ranges vs ip rack), minor filler words preserved.
